headline: Computational drug-target mapping: network pharmacology, curated databases, neural design
label: Computational Drug Target Mapping
summary: Network-level and neural approaches now map multi-target and interactome relationships, alongside curated resources for sodium channel modulators.
synthesis: The three items share a computational emphasis on mapping drug-target relationships rather than scoring single targets in isolation. A knowledge-graph and network-pharmacology pipeline links multi-target mechanisms of single Ayurvedic herbal drugs to diabetes and obesity. A fragment-based neural network proposes JAK2 and GLP-1R drug candidates and maps drug-target interactomes with in silico binding analysis. NavDB contributes a different layer: an open-access curated database of 8023 records covering 5168 voltage-gated sodium channel modulators and targets, with search and peptide matching. The dominant thread is network-level and neural prediction of target interactions; the database supplies curated data infrastructure rather than a predictive model, so the items differ in method even where they converge on interactome-scale questions.
